question: Does the publicly indexed SSRN record for the Viray Watershed study provide fish evidence usable for Pangasinan's freshwater inventory?

method.summary: Reviewed the SSRN indexed abstract and bibliographic metadata and cross-checked the item's posted-content/preprint status against its ResearchGate metadata page. The SSRN abstract page and its linked 33-page PDF could not be opened by the available web reader (403); no full text, tables, methods, supplements, raw data, or license statement were reviewed or retained.
method.accessFinding: The SSRN indexed record identifies a 33-page work posted 2025-09-09. Direct access to the abstract page and linked PDF returned 403 in this review. ResearchGate labels the item a preprint and offers no full-text file; peer review was not established.
method.abstractFinding: The abstract says six native fish species were identified in the Viray Watershed and names Eleotris melanosoma, Exyrias puntang, Glossogobius giuris, Glossogobius celebius, Rhinogobius bucculentus, and Glossogobius aureus. It does not expose fish-sampling dates, methods, stations, species-by-station results, counts, vouchers/accessions, coordinates, or a fish data file.
method.timeAndLocalityLimit: The abstract mentions land-cover change from 2010 to 2020, but does not establish that this is the fish sampling period. The study title identifies Viray Watershed, Pangasinan Province; station numbers referenced for water-quality results are not a fish-event or species-to-station crosswalk. No individual river, stream, reach, municipality, or coordinates can be assigned from the accessible abstract.
method.reuseFinding: No item-specific reuse license or redistribution permission was verified. No article prose beyond short bibliographic metadata, tables, figures, photos, or full-text content was copied. Publication and app reuse approval remain false.

waterbodyLead.habitatLane: freshwater watershed; constituent waterbodies and reaches unresolved

publication.citation: Alejo, K. G., Cui, L. E., Faustino-Eslava, D. V., & Villanueva-Peyraube, J. D. (2025). Guarding a Pristine Watershed: Baselining Water and Sediment Quality, Fish Diversity, and Land Use in Viray Watershed, Pangasinan Province, Philippines. SSRN posted content, posted 2025-09-09. https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5463460.
publication.accessStatus: Indexed abstract reviewed; SSRN page and PDF returned 403 to the web reader; full text not reviewed.
publication.peerReviewStatus: Not established; ResearchGate metadata categorizes the work as a preprint.
publication.license: No item-specific license or redistribution grant verified.

interpretation: Treat the six names only as abstract-reported labels from a posted research item. Without methods, collection events, station links, or vouchers, this screen does not verify the sampled organisms or establish species occurrence in a named river or stream.

The watershed title and provincial attribution support a freshwater source-discovery lead only; they do not provide constituent waterbody identities, locality geometry, municipality assignment, or reach extent.

The abstract's water-quality statements are not a current safety assessment. No fishing access, legal status, abundance, catchability, diet, conservation-status, or current-presence claim is derived from this screen.
No species assertions, occurrence rows, counts, waterbody assignments, coordinates, geometry, photographs, or public app content were added. Region I and Luzon remain incomplete.

decision.reason: The indexed abstract is a useful freshwater source lead, but direct full-text retrieval failed and the abstract lacks fish-event methods, site crosswalks, vouchers, and verified reuse terms.

nextAction: If independently accessible, obtain the author-accepted or publisher copy and review fish sampling method, collection dates, exact station/waterbody names, taxon-to-site evidence, vouchers/accessions, and item-specific reuse terms. If full text remains inaccessible, keep the six strings as abstract-only leads and continue the Pangasinan inland-water source sweep.
